Class TextUtils

java.lang.Object
outpututils.TextUtils
public class TextUtils extends Object
Helpers for terminal text output: a typewriter effect, short pauses, and 24-bit ANSI color formatting.

The color methods return strings containing ANSI escape codes and do not print anything themselves. They require a terminal that supports 24-bit ("truecolor") ANSI colors; other terminals may show approximate colors or stray escape characters.

Example: 

TextUtils.typewriterText(TextUtils.colorizeString("Hello!", "#00FFAA") + "\n", 30);
TextUtils.pause(500);

  • Method Details

    • typewriterText

      public static final void typewriterText(String message)
      Prints a message one character at a time with a default delay of 50 milliseconds between characters.

      Every char is delayed, including the invisible characters of ANSI escape sequences, so a string produced by one of the colorizeString methods may pause unevenly. If the thread is interrupted, the stack trace is printed and the remaining characters are not printed.

      Parameters:
      message - the text to print

    • typewriterText

      public static final void typewriterText(String message, int delay)
      Prints a message one character at a time with a custom delay between characters.

      See typewriterText(String) for notes on escape sequences and interruption.

      Parameters:
      message - the text to print
      delay - the delay after each character, in milliseconds; must not be negative, or Thread.sleep(long) throws an IllegalArgumentException

    • colorizeString

      public static final String colorizeString(String messageString, String hexCode) throws IllegalArgumentException
      Wraps a string in a 24-bit foreground color, given as a hex code, followed by a reset code.

      The hex code must contain exactly six hex digits (for example "#FF8800" or "ff8800"). Three-digit shorthand such as "#F80" is not supported.

      Parameters:
      messageString - the text to color
      hexCode - the color as RRGGBB, with or without a leading #; must not be null
      Returns:
      the colorized string, ready to print
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the hex code (excluding any #) is not six characters long, or contains characters that are not hex digits (NumberFormatException is a subclass of this exception). throws if hexCode is null

      Wraps a string in a 24-bit color foreground and background color escape codes, with other ANSI formatter options such as bolding or italics supports

      fgGreen - the foreground green component, 0 to 255

      bgGreen - the background green component, 0 to 255
      bgBlue - the background blue component, 0 to 255
